tools.semantics: An allowlist. Resolved AFTER disallowedTools against whatever that leaves. Accepts MCP server patterns mcp__<server> and mcp__<server>__*, which span the whole server including its write tools. Agent(type) restricts which subagent types may be spawned, but the parenthesised list binds only for an agent running as the main thread; in a subagent definition it is ignored.

disallowedTools.semantics: A denylist, applied FIRST; tools is then resolved against the remaining pool. An entry carrying a specifier removes the whole tool, not only the matching invocations - so Bash(git push *) here removes Bash entirely, and a later attempt to grant Bash(git show:*) through tools resolves to nothing.

main_thread_self_detection.semantics: Whether a running agent can observe that it is or is not the main thread. It cannot, by any means this project could find or measure. Environment is not it: a dispatched subagent's environment was captured and is byte-identical to its parent's - all 49 CLAUDE_*/ANTHROPIC_* variables present with identical values, including CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. The host does track this internally (agentDepth is threaded through the binary's tool-filter function alongside agentType and permissionMode, and spawnDepth is recorded per task) but does not surface it to the agent. What IS observable is the consequence: an agent whose definition grants a tool can check whether that tool is actually present in its toolset. That is the basis for a fail-closed check that does not require knowing one's own depth.

provenance.source: probe run 2026-09-17: parent and dispatched-subagent environments captured and diffed; binary strings at /opt/claude-code/bin/claude inspected
provenance.quote: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1
provenance.caveat: A verified negative for environment variables specifically, plus absence from the sub-agent and plugin references. Not proof that no mechanism exists anywhere in the host - an undocumented API or a hook payload field could still carry it.

hook_agent_identity.semantics: What a PreToolUse hook receives as agent_type. Carried by an agent HAVING an identity, not by it being a subagent: a dispatched subagent reports agent_type and agent_id; an agent launched as its own process with --agent reports agent_type and no agent_id; an ordinary main session with no --agent reports neither. A plugin agent reports its namespaced name, which role_for()'s rsplit(':', 1)[-1] resolves to the same role either way. Identity-aware guards therefore keep working when a worker is launched as a process rather than dispatched as a subagent - which is what makes script dispatch viable.

provenance.source: probe run 2026-09-17: a logging PreToolUse hook in a throwaway workspace across four launch shapes (main session, dispatched subagent, --agent with a project agent, --agent with an installed plugin agent)

nested.gate: Two conditions, both necessary. (1) Agent present in the dispatched agent's own tools allowlist. (2) CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH high enough to reach that depth - at the cap the Agent tool is withheld from the subagent's toolset entirely rather than offered and refused.

provenance.source: A/B probe, 2026-09-17: two fresh `claude -p` processes differing only in CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH, each asked to dispatch a subagent that reports whether it holds the Agent tool
provenance.quote: cap=2 -> HAVE_AGENT; cap=1 -> NO_AGENT
provenance.caveat: Nesting works and the environment variable is what controls it - both directions measured, not inferred from one. But the variable's DEFAULT is a remotely-controlled feature value (maxSubagentSpawnDepthFromGrowthBook, integer >= 1), so absent an explicit setting this capability is not under local control and can change with no local change at all. The value must be read at process start: exporting it into a running session does nothing, which is why the probe launched fresh processes. max_depth is null because there is no host constant to record - only whatever the environment is currently configured to allow.

provenance.caveat: The parenthesised type list binds only for an agent running as the main thread with claude --agent. In subagent definitions the list is ignored - so root must be a main-thread agent for the restriction to be real.

No inter-agent message primitive was found for plugin-shipped agents in either reference. Recorded as unsourced rather than false: this project has not demonstrated absence, only failed to find one. A portable envelope supplies it either way.
